methods.limits: FFmpeg takes the output format from the file ending; a plain command skips frame-rate, size and palette steps.

methods.steps: ffmpeg -i input.webm frame%04d.png; then gifski -o anim.gif frame*.png
methods.limits: Gifski's documentation names --width and --height as the biggest levers for a smaller file and --quality for lowering quality; on Windows the frame pattern may need %%04d.
Windows-oriented texture utility; check multi-image resource handling.

methods.steps: Load the DDS; File > Export As; name texture.png; click Export to open the PNG options.
methods.limits: GIMP loads DDS from version 2.10.10 on.
The format list marks DDS readable and writable, with DXT and mipmap options, and notes PNG needs libpng.

methods.steps: cwebp -q 80 input.jpg -o output.webp; alternatively cwebp -lossless input.jpg -o output.webp
methods.limits: -q runs from 0 to 100 and defaults to 75; lossless preserves what was decoded, not what the JPG discarded; the manual lists JPEG as an accepted input.

methods.steps: Open the JPG; File > Export As; give a name ending .webp; tick Lossless or set the image quality and alpha quality sliders.
methods.limits: Higher quality usually means a larger file.
WebP needs the WEBP delegate library.
-map gives manual control of which stream is used, -vn turns video off, and the build needs LAME.
The track ID comes from mkvmerge --identify; the stream is written as stored, so the result is a playable MP3 only when the track is already MP3.
The format list calls the JPEG entry the JFIF format and marks it readable and writable; PNG needs libpng.
Size and quality settings are not repeated; -movflags +faststart moves the moov atom to the front in a second pass.

methods.steps: Open Source on the toolbar; pick the WMV; choose a preset such as Fast 1080p30; set Save As and the To folder; Start.
methods.limits: The source-formats page lists WMV; Fast 1080p30 writes MP4 with H.264 and AAC stereo.

methods.steps: Open HEIF; File > Export; choose JPEG in Format; save.
methods.limits: Compatible macOS and decodable HEIF required.
The output format comes from the filename suffix; a quality option applies to JPEG; a file with several images gives numbered outputs ending -1, -2.

methods.steps: Open SVG as an image; File > Export As; use drawing.jpg; confirm JPEG options.
methods.limits: SVG is rasterized at import; retain vector original.
The format list gives SVG read and write mode and says it renders with Inkscape, RSVG or its internal MSVG renderer.

methods.steps: In Inkscape, File > Export PNG Image; choose the area and image size in pixels; pick a file name; click Export. Open the PNG in Preview and choose File > Export > Format JPEG.
methods.limits: Two-stage macOS workflow with a PNG intermediate.

methods.steps: Open the PNG; File > Export As; name ending .gif; choose Interlace, comment and As animation options in the GIF dialog.
methods.limits: GIMP only exports a maximum of 256 colors; its docs advise indexed mode first.
The format list marks PNG and GIF read and write, with GIF as 8-bit PseudoColor up to 256 palette entries.

methods.steps: Save a text file ending in .svg with an svg element carrying width, height and xmlns http://www.w3.org/2000/svg; inside it add an image element with href set to the JPEG's file name and width and height set to the picture's pixel size; open it in a browser.
methods.limits: JPEG, PNG and other SVG files are the formats SVG software must support; width and height are required; the SVG links the JPEG, so the two files stay together.
